objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3 sqlite3;
objects.description: Opaque handle for a database connection to an SQLite database. Created by sqlite3_open*() and destroyed by sqlite3_close*(). Used as the root object for most API calls.
VFS-level open file handle. Embeds a pointer to an sqlite3_io_methods vtable that implements I/O for the file. Typically subclassed by VFS implementations to append private fields.
VFS virtual-method table defining all I/O operations for an sqlite3_file. Implemented by VFSes. iVersion gates availability of later methods.
Virtual File System descriptor linking SQLite core to OS-specific file and dynamic loading services. VFSes register via sqlite3_vfs_register.
Pluggable memory allocator vtable. Used with sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_MALLOC/GETMALLOC) to override allocator.

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_stmt sqlite3_stmt;
objects.description: Opaque prepared statement object representing compiled SQL. Created by sqlite3_prepare*(), finalized by sqlite3_finalize().

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_value sqlite3_value;
objects.description: Dynamically typed SQLite value container passed into SQL functions and used for column/parameter values. Managed by SQLite unless duplicated.

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_context sqlite3_context;
objects.description: Execution context for an SQL function (scalar/aggregate/window). Passed to user-defined functions to set results and get aux data.

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_mutex sqlite3_mutex;
objects.description: Opaque handle for SQLite mutex objects used for internal or application-level synchronization (when mutexes enabled).

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_pcache sqlite3_pcache;
objects.description: Opaque handle for a custom page cache instance for the pager layer provided via sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_PCACHE2).
Represents a single page within a custom page cache: pBuf is content buffer; pExtra is per-page extra storage.
Pluggable page cache method table to override default pager cache. Registered through sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_PCACHE2).
Obsolete custom page cache vtable retained for backwards compatibility.

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_backup sqlite3_backup;
objects.description: Opaque handle for an online backup operation between two connections. Created by sqlite3_backup_init(), finalized by sqlite3_backup_finish().

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_api_routines sqlite3_api_routines;
objects.description: Table of function pointers that exposes the SQLite C API to loadable extensions. Supplied to extension entry point.
Signed/unsigned 64-bit integer typedefs for cross-platform use. sqlite3_int64/sqlite3_uint64 are preferred; sqlite_int64/sqlite_uint64 kept for compatibility.
Vtable to supply custom mutex implementation via sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_MUTEX/GETMUTEX).
Base struct for a virtual table instance. Virtual table implementations typically embed this as the first field and add more.
Base struct for a virtual table cursor. Implementations embed and extend this to maintain scan state.
Virtual table module method table defining callbacks SQLite uses to interact with a virtual table implementation.
Structure used by xBestIndex to receive WHERE/ORDER BY constraints and return a chosen index plan for virtual tables.

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_blob sqlite3_blob;
objects.description: Opaque handle for incremental BLOB I/O on a table column. Opened via sqlite3_blob_open() and closed via sqlite3_blob_close().
Context passed to legacy R*Tree geometry callbacks, providing parameters and user data for the geometry function.
Extended context for R*Tree 2nd-gen query callbacks, exposing node/entry coordinates, levels, and result scoring fields.
FTS5 extension API vtable provided to custom FTS5 auxiliary functions to inspect the current match context and fetch document/query data.

objects.definition: typedef struct Fts5Context Fts5Context;
objects.description: Opaque context passed to FTS5 extension functions; used with Fts5ExtensionApi to query row/phrase information.

objects.definition:
typedef struct Fts5PhraseIter Fts5PhraseIter;
struct Fts5PhraseIter { const unsigned char *a; const unsigned char *b; };
objects.description: Iterator state for enumerating FTS5 phrase occurrences across columns/positions via Fts5ExtensionApi xPhraseFirst/Next methods.
FTS5 tokenizer vtable for custom tokenizers providing xCreate/xDelete/xTokenize callbacks.

objects.definition: typedef struct Fts5Tokenizer Fts5Tokenizer;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a specific tokenizer instance used by FTS5 tokenizers; created by fts5_tokenizer.xCreate and used in xTokenize.
Entry API for FTS5 extensions to register custom tokenizers and auxiliary functions with the FTS5 module.
Scalar type used in R*Tree callbacks for coordinate parameters. Either double or 64-bit int depending on build.
Opaque handle representing a specific WAL database snapshot to start read transactions at. Created by sqlite3_snapshot_get(), used by sqlite3_snapshot_open(), freed by sqlite3_snapshot_free().

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_str sqlite3_str;
objects.description: Opaque dynamic string builder used with sqlite3_str_* APIs to safely assemble dynamically-sized strings.

objects.definition: typedef int (*sqlite3_loadext_entry)(sqlite3 *db, char **pzErrMsg, const sqlite3_api_routines *pThunk);
objects.description: Function pointer type for extension entry point. While not a struct/enum/class, this typedef defines the pointer type used when loading extensions.

functions.name: sqlite3_libversion
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a UTF-8 string literal containing the SQLite runtime library version (e.g., "3.39.0"). Useful to verify runtime vs. headers.
requirements: Must not free or modify the returned pointer; it is managed by SQLite
Thread-safe

functions.name: sqlite3_sourceid
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a UTF-8 string literal identifying the source check-in (date/time and SHA hash) of the SQLite library in use.
requirements: Do not free or modify the returned pointer; managed by SQLite
Thread-safe

functions.name: sqlite3_libversion_number
functions.description: Returns the SQLite runtime version number as an integer (X*1000000 + Y*1000 + Z).
requirements: Thread-safe

functions.name: sqlite3_compileoption_used
functions.description: Returns 1 if the named compile-time option was used to build the SQLite library, 0 otherwise. The SQLITE_ prefix may be omitted in zOptName.
requirements: zOptName must be a valid NUL-terminated UTF-8 string pointer
If compiled with SQLITE_OMIT_COMPILEOPTION_DIAGS, function is a stub macro returning 0

functions.name: sqlite3_compileoption_get
functions.description: Returns the N-th compile-time option string (without the SQLITE_ prefix), or NULL if N is out of range. Allows iterating all options.
requirements: N must be >= 0; if out-of-range returns NULL
Returned pointer must not be freed
If compiled with SQLITE_OMIT_COMPILEOPTION_DIAGS, it is a stub macro returning NULL

functions.name: sqlite3_threadsafe
functions.description: Returns non-zero if SQLite was compiled with mutexing enabled (SQLITE_THREADSAFE=1 or 2). Returns 0 if compiled without mutexing.
requirements: Reports compile-time setting only; not affected by sqlite3_config() runtime modes

functions.name: sqlite3_close
functions.description: Closes and destroys a database connection. Returns SQLITE_OK on success, or SQLITE_BUSY if there are unfinalized prepared statements, open BLOBs, or unfinished backups; in that case the connection remains open.
requirements: Argument must be a NULL pointer or a valid sqlite3* obtained from sqlite3_open(), sqlite3_open16(), or sqlite3_open_v2()
Caller must finalize all prepared statements, close all BLOB handles, and finish all backups before calling, or use sqlite3_close_v2() instead
Calling with NULL is a no-op

functions.name: sqlite3_close
functions.description: Closes (destroys) an open sqlite3 database connection and frees associated resources. Returns SQLITE_OK on success. If there are any unfinalized prepared statements, open BLOB handles, or unfinished backup objects, this function leaves the connection open and returns SQLITE_BUSY. Use sqlite3_close_v2() if you need GC‑friendly semantics (it defers deallocation). Calling with NULL is a no-op.
requirements: The argument must be a pointer obtained from sqlite3_open(), sqlite3_open16(), or sqlite3_open_v2(), and not previously closed.

All prepared statements must be finalized (sqlite3_finalize), all BLOB handles closed (sqlite3_blob_close), and all backups finished (sqlite3_backup_finish) before calling, otherwise SQLITE_BUSY is returned and the connection remains open.
It is safe to pass NULL (no-op).
If a transaction is open, it is automatically rolled back on successful close.

functions.name: sqlite3_close_v2
functions.description: Closes a database connection. Returns SQLITE_OK even if there are unfinalized statements/BLOBs/backups; the connection becomes a "zombie" and is deallocated automatically when they are all finalized/closed/finished.
requirements: Argument must be a NULL or valid sqlite3* opened by sqlite3_open()/16/_v2() and not previously closed
Calling with NULL is a no-op
Further use of the zombie connection is invalid

functions.name: sqlite3_close_v2
functions.description: Closes (destroys) an sqlite3 database connection with deferred cleanup semantics suitable for GC'd languages. Returns SQLITE_OK even if there are unfinalized statements, open BLOBs, or unfinished backups; in that case the connection becomes a “zombie” and is automatically deallocated when all associated objects are finalized/closed/finished. Calling with NULL is a no-op.
requirements: The argument must be a pointer obtained from sqlite3_open(), sqlite3_open16(), or sqlite3_open_v2(), and not previously closed.
The connection must not be used again after calling sqlite3_close_v2(); it becomes unusable (zombie) until automatically deallocated.
It is safe to pass NULL (no-op).
If a transaction is open when the object is ultimately destroyed, it will be rolled back.

functions.name: sqlite3_exec
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_exec(sqlite3*, const char *sql, int (*callback)(void*,int,char**,char**), void *, char **errmsg);
functions.description: Convenience API to execute UTF-8 SQL text (possibly with multiple semicolon-separated statements). Optionally invokes a row callback per result row. On error, stops the current statement, skips subsequent statements, and sets *errmsg to a heap-allocated message (caller must sqlite3_free()).
requirements: First parameter must be a valid, open sqlite3* that remains open for the duration of the call
sql must point to UTF-8 SQL; must not be modified while running
If callback is non-NULL, it must be reentrant-safe with respect to using the same db connection only per SQLite guarantees
Do not close the database from within the callback
If errmsg is non-NULL and an error occurs, caller must sqlite3_free(*errmsg) when done
Callback returning non-zero aborts execution and causes SQLITE_ABORT

functions.name: sqlite3_initialize
functions.description: Initializes the SQLite library (mutexes, VFS, global state). Usually called automatically. Returns SQLITE_OK or an error code.
requirements: Thread-safe
Calling multiple times is a no-op except first effective call
May be required explicitly if compiled with SQLITE_OMIT_AUTOINIT

functions.name: sqlite3_shutdown
functions.description: Shuts down the SQLite library and releases resources from sqlite3_initialize(). Not thread-safe; must be called from a single thread after closing all database connections and deallocating all SQLite resources.
requirements: All database connections must be closed and SQLite resources deallocated before calling
Not thread-safe; call from a single thread
Subsequent use requires sqlite3_initialize() again

functions.name: sqlite3_os_init
functions.description: Performs OS-specific SQLite initialization. Called by sqlite3_initialize(). Applications should not call directly except on custom builds (SQLITE_OS_OTHER).
requirements: Only for custom builds when required; otherwise do not call directly
Must return SQLITE_OK on success; error codes indicate failure

functions.name: sqlite3_os_end
functions.description: Undoes OS-specific initialization done by sqlite3_os_init(). Called by sqlite3_shutdown(). Applications should not call directly except on custom builds.
requirements: Only for custom builds when required; otherwise do not call directly
Must return SQLITE_OK on success

functions.name: sqlite3_config
functions.description: Global library configuration. Must be called before sqlite3_initialize() (or after sqlite3_shutdown()). Accepts a verb and associated arguments to configure global behavior (memory allocators, mutexes, logging, threading mode, etc.).
requirements: Not thread-safe; ensure no other SQLite APIs are running concurrently
May only be called before sqlite3_initialize() or after sqlite3_shutdown()
Arguments depend on the configuration verb; passing wrong types leads to SQLITE_MISUSE
Check return code for SQLITE_OK

functions.name: sqlite3_db_config
functions.description: Configures behavior of a single database connection (e.g., lookaside memory, foreign keys, triggers, WAL close checkpoint behavior).
requirements: First argument must be a valid sqlite3*
Only certain verbs are accepted; arguments must match the verb’s signature
Returns SQLITE_OK only if the change is successful; otherwise an error code

functions.name: sqlite3_enable_shared_cache
functions.description: Enables or disables process-wide shared pager cache mode. Deprecated and discouraged. Returns SQLITE_OK or SQLITE_MISUSE on some platforms (e.g., macOS/iOS; always returns SQLITE_MISUSE there).
requirements: Affects subsequent sqlite3_open* calls only
Not recommended; prefer per-connection shared cache via sqlite3_open_v2() flags

functions.name: sqlite3_release_memory
functions.description: Attempts to free N bytes of heap memory by deallocating non-essential caches used by SQLite. Returns number of bytes actually freed (may be >, <, or == N). No-op if memory management disabled.
requirements: Thread-safe
Caller must not assume exact amount freed

functions.name: sqlite3_db_release_memory
functions.description: Attempts to free as much heap memory as possible associated with the specified database connection.
requirements: sqlite3* must be valid
Returns SQLITE_OK

functions.name: sqlite3_db_release_memory
functions.description: Attempts to free as much heap memory as possible used by the specified database connection (e.g., caches). Unlike sqlite3_release_memory(), this works regardless of SQLITE_ENABLE_MEMORY_MANAGEMENT. Returns an SQLite result code (SQLITE_OK on success).
requirements: db must be a valid open sqlite3* connection.
May be called at any time; does not change database content.
Return code should be checked for success.

functions.name: sqlite3_soft_heap_limit64
functions.description: Sets (and/or queries) the soft upper bound on heap memory (in bytes) used by SQLite. SQLite strives to stay under the soft limit by releasing caches; it will exceed the limit rather than fail allocations. Returns the prior limit.
requirements: Pass N<0 to query without change; N=0 disables limiter
Soft limit may be constrained by hard heap limit if set

functions.name: sqlite3_soft_heap_limit64
functions.description: Sets or queries the process-wide soft heap memory limit used by SQLite. SQLite attempts to keep heap usage under this advisory limit by trimming caches. Passing N<0 leaves the limit unchanged; N==0 disables the soft limit; otherwise sets it to N bytes. Returns the prior soft limit (or negative on error).
requirements: This is a global setting affecting all connections in the process.
If N is negative, the soft limit is not changed; use the return value to query current limit.
If set higher than the hard heap limit (if any), it is truncated to the hard limit.

functions.name: sqlite3_hard_heap_limit64
functions.description: Sets (and/or queries) a hard upper bound on memory used by SQLite. Unlike soft limit, allocations fail when limit is reached. Returns the prior limit.
requirements: Pass N<0 to query without change; N=0 disables hard limit
Soft limit adjusted to be ≤ hard limit

functions.name: sqlite3_hard_heap_limit64
functions.description: Sets or queries the process-wide hard heap memory limit used by SQLite. If the hard limit is enabled (N>0), memory allocations that would exceed it fail with SQLITE_NOMEM. Passing N<0 leaves the limit unchanged; N==0 disables the hard limit. Returns the prior hard limit (or negative on error). When a hard limit is set, the soft limit is automatically enabled and adjusted to be within [1..N] if necessary.
requirements: This is a global setting affecting all connections in the process.
If N is negative, the hard limit is not changed; use the return value to query current limit.
If enabling the hard limit, be aware allocations beyond N will fail; code should handle SQLITE_NOMEM.
Setting the hard limit may also adjust the soft limit into the range [1..N].

functions.name: sqlite3_clear_bindings
functions.description: Resets all parameter bindings on a prepared statement to NULL, without resetting the statement itself.
requirements: Statement must be a valid sqlite3_stmt*
Returns SQLITE_OK on success

functions.name: sqlite3_last_insert_rowid
functions.description: Returns the rowid of the most recent successful INSERT into a rowid table on the given connection (or 0 if none).
requirements: Connection must be valid
Value may change due to triggers or virtual tables; see header docs

functions.name: sqlite3_set_last_insert_rowid
functions.description: Overrides the value returned by sqlite3_last_insert_rowid() for the given connection.
requirements: Connection must be valid

functions.name: sqlite3_set_last_insert_rowid
functions.description: Sets the last insert rowid for a connection (duplicate entry included earlier).
requirements: Connection must be valid

functions.name: sqlite3_changes
functions.description: Returns number of database rows changed, inserted or deleted by the most recently completed DML statement on the connection (not including trigger side-effects). Undefined if count exceeds int.
requirements: Connection must be valid
Concurrent changes on same connection make return value unpredictable

functions.name: sqlite3_changes64
functions.description: 64-bit version of sqlite3_changes(). Returns number of rows changed by last DML.
requirements: Connection must be valid

functions.name: sqlite3_total_changes
functions.description: Returns total number of rows inserted, modified or deleted by all DML statements since the connection was opened. Undefined if exceeds int.
requirements: Connection must be valid

functions.name: sqlite3_total_changes64
functions.description: 64-bit total changes counter since connection open.
requirements: Connection must be valid

functions.name: sqlite3_interrupt
functions.description: Requests that any running operation on the connection abort at its earliest opportunity, causing it to return SQLITE_INTERRUPT. Affects currently running and any statements started until the running count drops to zero.
requirements: Connection must remain valid until the call returns
It is safe to call from a different thread than the one executing the SQL

functions.name: sqlite3_complete
functions.description: Returns 1 if the UTF-8 input appears to form a complete SQL statement (ends with a semicolon token and not a CREATE TRIGGER prefix), 0 if incomplete, or SQLITE_NOMEM on OOM.
requirements: sql must be a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string pointer (may be NULL for 0)
Does not parse SQL for syntax correctness

functions.name: sqlite3_complete16
functions.description: UTF-16 version of sqlite3_complete() (native byte order).
requirements: sql must be NUL-terminated UTF-16 in native byte order
May auto-initialize; if autoinit fails, non-zero may be returned regardless of completeness

functions.name: sqlite3_busy_handler
functions.description: Registers a busy-handler callback invoked when a table/file lock prevents progress. The callback receives the user pointer and a retry count; if it returns non-zero, SQLite retries the operation after a delay; returning 0 aborts with SQLITE_BUSY.
requirements: Only one busy handler per connection; registering replaces any previous handler
Callback must not reenter or modify the same connection (not reentrant)
Must not close the connection or statements from within the handler

functions.name: sqlite3_busy_timeout
functions.description: Convenience to set a busy handler that sleeps and retries until at least ms milliseconds of waiting accumulate, then fails with SQLITE_BUSY. Pass ≤0 to clear any busy handler.
requirements: Only one busy handler per connection; replaces any set via sqlite3_busy_handler

functions.name: sqlite3_get_table
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_get_table(sqlite3 *db, const char *zSql, char ***pazResult, int *pnRow, int *pnColumn, char **pzErrmsg);
functions.description: Legacy convenience API that executes the SQL and returns an entire result table as an array of UTF-8 strings (first row column names, followed by row data). Caller must free using sqlite3_free_table().
requirements: db must be valid and open
zSql must be UTF-8; may contain multiple statements
Do not call sqlite3_free() directly on result; must use sqlite3_free_table()
If pzErrmsg not NULL on error, caller must sqlite3_free(*pzErrmsg)

functions.name: sqlite3_free_table
functions.description: Frees a table result allocated by sqlite3_get_table().
requirements: Pass the same pointer returned by sqlite3_get_table(), or NULL (no-op)
Do not use for other memory

functions.name: sqlite3_mprintf
functions.description: Formats a string similarly to printf() and returns it in memory allocated via sqlite3_malloc64(). Caller must sqlite3_free() the result. Supports SQLite-specific formats like %q, %Q, %w, %z.
requirements: Returned pointer must be freed with sqlite3_free()
Returns NULL on allocation failure

functions.name: sqlite3_vmprintf
functions.description: va_list variant of sqlite3_mprintf().
requirements: Returned pointer must be freed with sqlite3_free()
Returns NULL on allocation failure

functions.name: sqlite3_snprintf
functions.description: Writes formatted output into provided buffer (size n includes NUL). Returns the buffer pointer. Always NUL-terminates if n>0. Note parameter order differs from C99 snprintf.
requirements: Buffer must be at least 1 byte to guarantee NUL termination
Return is pointer to buffer, not number of characters written

functions.name: sqlite3_vsnprintf
functions.signature: SQLITE_API char *sqlite3_vsnprintf(int, char*, const char*, va_list);
functions.description: va_list variant of sqlite3_snprintf().
requirements: Same as sqlite3_snprintf

functions.name: sqlite3_malloc
functions.description: Allocates at least N bytes using SQLite’s allocator (8-byte aligned by default). Returns NULL if N<=0 or on OOM.
requirements: Free with sqlite3_free()
Do not mix with system malloc/free

functions.name: sqlite3_malloc64
functions.description: 64-bit size variant of sqlite3_malloc().
requirements: Free with sqlite3_free()

functions.name: sqlite3_realloc
functions.description: Reallocates a prior sqlite3_malloc/realloc block to at least N bytes. If ptr is NULL behaves like sqlite3_malloc(). If N<=0 frees ptr and returns NULL. On failure returns NULL and leaves original allocation intact.
requirements: Pointer must be from sqlite3_malloc/sqlite3_realloc
Free with sqlite3_free() when done

functions.name: sqlite3_realloc64
functions.description: 64-bit size variant of sqlite3_realloc().
requirements: Pointer must be from sqlite3_malloc/sqlite3_realloc

functions.name: sqlite3_free
functions.description: Frees memory allocated by SQLite’s allocation routines. Safe to pass NULL (no-op).
requirements: Pointer must be from sqlite3_malloc/sqlite3_realloc/sqlite3_mprintf/related

functions.name: sqlite3_msize
functions.description: Returns the allocated size in bytes of a memory block previously obtained from sqlite3_malloc/sqlite3_realloc. Returns 0 if X is NULL.
requirements: Pointer must refer to a valid, not-yet-freed allocation from SQLite’s allocator

functions.name: sqlite3_memory_used
functions.description: Returns the current number of bytes of memory outstanding (allocated but not freed) by SQLite’s allocator.
requirements: Requires memstatus tracking unless compiled with SQLITE_DEFAULT_MEMSTATUS=0 and disabled via config

functions.name: sqlite3_memory_highwater
functions.description: Returns the high-water mark of sqlite3_memory_used(). If resetFlag is non-zero, resets the high-water mark to current usage after returning the prior value.

functions.name: sqlite3_randomness
functions.description: Fills P with N bytes of pseudo-random data. If insufficient prior calls, seeds from VFS xRandomness first call.
requirements: P may be NULL; function becomes a no-op when N<=0 or P==NULL

functions.name: sqlite3_set_authorizer
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_set_authorizer(sqlite3*, int (*xAuth)(void*,int,const char*,const char*,const char*,const char*), void *pUserData);
functions.description: Registers or disables a compile-time authorization callback invoked during statement compilation to allow/deny SQL operations or ignore certain column reads.
requirements: Only one authorizer per connection; setting replaces previous
Callback must not modify or close the same database connection (not reentrant)
Return only SQLITE_OK, SQLITE_DENY, or SQLITE_IGNORE; other returns cause prepare to fail
Keep authorizer installed during sqlite3_step() if reprepare might occur

functions.name: sqlite3_trace
functions.signature: SQLITE_API SQLITE_DEPRECATED void *sqlite3_trace(sqlite3*, void(*xTrace)(void*,const char*), void*);
functions.description: Deprecated API that sets a trace callback invoked with the SQL text as a statement begins executing. Use sqlite3_trace_v2() instead.
requirements: Replaced by sqlite3_trace_v2()
Not reentrant; callback must not call SQLite APIs that reenter connection

functions.name: sqlite3_profile
functions.signature: SQLITE_API SQLITE_DEPRECATED void *sqlite3_profile(sqlite3*, void(*xProfile)(void*,const char*,sqlite3_uint64), void*);
functions.description: Deprecated API to register a callback invoked when each SQL statement finishes, with the SQL text and approximate nanosecond duration. Superseded by sqlite3_trace_v2().
requirements: Callback must be threadsafe if connection used multi-threaded

functions.name: sqlite3_trace_v2
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_trace_v2(sqlite3*, unsigned uMask, int(*xCallback)(unsigned,void*,void*,void*), void *pCtx);
functions.description: Registers or clears a tracing callback with specified event mask (SQLITE_TRACE_*). The callback receives event type, context pointer, and event-specific P/X pointers. Return value from callback currently ignored (should return 0).
requirements: Passing NULL callback or mask==0 disables tracing
Overrides any prior trace/profile callback
Callback must not assume P/X types beyond documented event type

functions.name: sqlite3_progress_handler
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_progress_handler(sqlite3*, int N, int(*)(void*), void*);
functions.description: Registers a progress callback invoked periodically every N virtual machine instructions executed on the connection. Returning non-zero from the callback interrupts the operation (similar to sqlite3_interrupt).
requirements: Only one progress handler per connection; setting replaces previous
Callback must not modify or close the same connection (not reentrant)
Disable by passing N<1 or NULL callback

functions.name: sqlite3_open
functions.description: Opens the SQLite database file specified by UTF-8 filename (or :memory: or empty string for temp DB). On success returns SQLITE_OK and writes a database handle to *ppDb. On failure returns error code and may still set *ppDb to a partially-open connection for error introspection.
requirements: filename must be UTF-8 string pointer
Caller must close returned handle with sqlite3_close()/v2()
On failure you may call sqlite3_errmsg() on *ppDb if non-NULL

functions.name: sqlite3_open
functions.description: Opens an SQLite database file specified by a UTF‑8 filename and returns a database connection handle in *ppDb. Returns SQLITE_OK on success; otherwise an error code is returned. On most errors, *ppDb is set to a valid handle that can be queried for error details via sqlite3_errmsg(); on allocation failure, *ppDb may be NULL.
requirements: filename must be a UTF‑8 string. Special names include ":memory:" (in‑memory DB) and "" (temporary on‑disk DB).
After a successful open, the connection should be closed with sqlite3_close() or sqlite3_close_v2().
On Windows Runtime, a temporary directory must be set before opening if features requiring temp files are used.
Do not assume *ppDb is NULL on failure; only OOM guarantees NULL. Always close non‑NULL *ppDb with sqlite3_close/sqlite3_close_v2.
The default DB text encoding is UTF‑8 for sqlite3_open().

functions.name: sqlite3_open16
functions.description: UTF-16 (native byte order) version of sqlite3_open().
requirements: filename must be UTF-16 NUL-terminated
Close handle with sqlite3_close()/v2()

functions.name: sqlite3_open16
functions.description: Opens an SQLite database file specified by a UTF‑16 (native byte order) filename and returns a database connection handle in *ppDb. Returns SQLITE_OK on success; otherwise an error code. On most errors, *ppDb is set to a valid handle for error details; on allocation failure, *ppDb may be NULL. Databases created by sqlite3_open16() default to UTF‑16 encoding (native byte order).
requirements: filename must be a zero‑terminated UTF‑16 string in native byte order.
Close the returned connection with sqlite3_close() or sqlite3_close_v2().
Do not assume *ppDb is NULL on failure; close any non‑NULL handle.
Special names ":memory:" and "" behave as with sqlite3_open().

functions.name: sqlite3_open_v2
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_open_v2(const char *filename, sqlite3 **ppDb, int flags, const char *zVfs);
functions.description: Extended open with flags (READONLY/READWRITE/CREATE, URI, NOMUTEX/FULLMUTEX, shared/private cache, EXRESCODE, NOFOLLOW). zVfs selects a VFS by name or NULL for default.
requirements: flags must include exactly one of READONLY/READWRITE/(READWRITE|CREATE)
Some flags are VFS-only and ignored/unsupported for open_v2()
Do not pass SQLITE_OPEN_EXCLUSIVE (no-op historically)
On success caller must close handle
Use SQLITE_OPEN_URI to parse filename as URI

functions.name: sqlite3_open_v2
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_open_v2(const char *filename, sqlite3 **ppDb, int flags, const char *zVfs);
functions.description: Opens an SQLite database with additional control. The UTF‑8 filename may be a URI if SQLITE_OPEN_URI is used or URI handling is globally enabled. The flags must include exactly one of SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY, SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE, or (SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE|SQLITE_OPEN_CREATE), optionally OR’d with flags like SQLITE_OPEN_URI, SQLITE_OPEN_MEMORY, SQLITE_OPEN_NOMUTEX/FULLMUTEX, SQLITE_OPEN_SHAREDCACHE/PRIVATECACHE, SQLITE_OPEN_NOFOLLOW, SQLITE_OPEN_EXRESCODE, etc. zVfs names a specific VFS or may be NULL for the default. Returns SQLITE_OK on success; otherwise an error code (possibly extended if SQLITE_OPEN_EXRESCODE used). *ppDb may still be non‑NULL on failure (except OOM).
requirements: flags must include exactly one of: SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY, SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE, or (SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE|SQLITE_OPEN_CREATE).
Only documented optional flags should be used; do not rely on SQLITE_OPEN_EXCLUSIVE for POSIX O_EXCL semantics (it is a VFS‑only bit and historically a no‑op).
If SQLITE_OPEN_URI is not set, URIs are treated as filenames unless URI handling was globally enabled via sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_URI).
zVfs must be NULL or the name of a registered sqlite3_vfs.
Close returned connections with sqlite3_close()/sqlite3_close_v2().
Do not assume *ppDb is NULL on failure (except on OOM).

functions.description: Sets an error indicating an out-of-memory condition (SQLITE_NOMEM).

functions.name: sqlite3_result_error_code
functions.description: Sets the error code for the function error result. Subsequent sqlite3_result_error() may reset to SQLITE_ERROR.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_int
functions.description: Sets function result to 32-bit integer.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_int64
functions.description: Sets function result to 64-bit integer.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_null
functions.description: Sets function result to SQL NULL.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_text
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_text(sqlite3_context*, const char*, int, void(*)(void*));
functions.description: Sets function result to UTF-8 text string with destructor semantics analogous to sqlite3_result_blob(). If n<0 uses length up to first NUL.
requirements: If SQLITE_STATIC, lifetime must exceed SQLite use

functions.name: sqlite3_result_text64
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_text64(sqlite3_context*, const char*, sqlite3_uint64, void(*)(void*), unsigned char encoding);
functions.description: Sets function result to text with 64-bit length and explicit encoding (SQLITE_UTF8/UTF16*).
requirements: encoding must be valid (SQLITE_UTF8/SQLITE_UTF16/LE/BE)

functions.name: sqlite3_result_text16
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_text16(sqlite3_context*, const void*, int, void(*)(void*));
functions.description: Sets function result to UTF-16 (native) text.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_text16le
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_text16le(sqlite3_context*, const void*, int, void(*)(void*));
functions.description: Sets function result to UTF-16LE text.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_text16be
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_text16be(sqlite3_context*, const void*, int, void(*)(void*));
functions.description: Sets function result to UTF-16BE text.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_value
functions.description: Sets result to be a copy of the supplied sqlite3_value (SQLite makes its own copy).
requirements: sqlite3_value may be protected or unprotected; both accepted

functions.name: sqlite3_result_pointer
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_pointer(sqlite3_context*, void*, const char*, void(*)(void*));
functions.description: Sets result to a typed host-language pointer (NULL SQL value associated with P and type string). Optional destructor called when SQLite is finished with P.
requirements: Type string should be a static literal and must match in sqlite3_value_pointer() retrieval

functions.name: sqlite3_result_zeroblob
functions.description: Sets result to a zero-filled BLOB of n bytes (n may be negative to get zero-length BLOB). Intended for incremental blob I/O.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_zeroblob64
functions.description: 64-bit size version of sqlite3_result_zeroblob(); returns SQLITE_OK or error.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_subtype
functions.description: Sets the 8-bit subtype associated with the function result (for application-defined use).

functions.name: sqlite3_str_new
functions.description: Creates a dynamic string builder associated with a database’s limits (or global limits if db is NULL). Always returns a usable object; on OOM it becomes a special object that yields errors and NULL when finished.
requirements: Call sqlite3_str_finish() to obtain/finalize and free the builder

functions.name: sqlite3_str_finish
functions.description: Finalizes a dynamic string object, returning an allocated result string (or NULL on OOM or zero-length). Caller must sqlite3_free() the result.
requirements: Do not use the sqlite3_str* after calling finish

functions.name: sqlite3_str_appendf
functions.description: Appends formatted text to a dynamic string (SQLite printf formats).
requirements: Builder must be valid; on OOM the builder records error and future appends are ignored

functions.name: sqlite3_str_vappendf
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_str_vappendf(sqlite3_str*, const char *zFormat, va_list);
functions.description: va_list variant of sqlite3_str_appendf().

functions.name: sqlite3_str_append
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_str_append(sqlite3_str*, const char *zIn, int N);
functions.description: Appends exactly N bytes from zIn (may include NULs). If N<0 appends until first NUL.

functions.name: sqlite3_str_appendall
functions.description: Appends entire zero-terminated string zIn.

functions.name: sqlite3_str_appendchar
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_str_appendchar(sqlite3_str*, int N, char C);
functions.description: Appends N copies of character C.

functions.name: sqlite3_str_reset
functions.description: Resets the dynamic string to zero bytes; continues using same builder.

functions.name: sqlite3_str_errcode
functions.description: Returns SQLITE_OK if no error occurred while appending; otherwise the error code (typically SQLITE_NOMEM or SQLITE_TOOBIG).

functions.name: sqlite3_str_length
functions.description: Returns current byte length of the dynamic string (excluding final NUL).

functions.name: sqlite3_str_value
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the builder’s internal buffer (not finalized). The pointer may be invalidated by subsequent appends. Do not free.
requirements: Use only for inspection before finish; copy if persistence needed

functions.name: sqlite3_mutex_alloc
functions.description: Allocates and returns a mutex object. Argument selects type (FAST/RECURSIVE or one of SQLITE_MUTEX_STATIC_* for static mutexes). May return NULL if allocation fails.
requirements: Only dynamic mutexes (FAST/RECURSIVE) should be freed with sqlite3_mutex_free(); static mutexes must not be freed
Do not assume recursive behavior unless RECURSIVE is requested

functions.name: sqlite3_mutex_free
functions.description: Deallocates a dynamic mutex previously allocated by sqlite3_mutex_alloc(). Undefined behavior if used on static mutex types.
requirements: Argument must be a dynamic mutex or NULL (no-op)

functions.name: sqlite3_mutex_enter
functions.description: Enters (locks) the mutex, blocking if necessary.
requirements: Passing NULL is a no-op
For non-recursive mutexes, calling twice from same thread is undefined

functions.name: sqlite3_mutex_try
functions.description: Attempts to enter the mutex without blocking. Returns SQLITE_OK if successful, SQLITE_BUSY if not. On some platforms this may always return SQLITE_BUSY.
requirements: Passing NULL is a no-op that returns SQLITE_OK

functions.name: sqlite3_mutex_leave
functions.description: Leaves (unlocks) the mutex previously entered by the same thread.
requirements: Passing NULL is a no-op
Behavior undefined if the calling thread does not own the mutex

functions.name: sqlite3_mutex_held
functions.description: For debug builds, returns true if the mutex is currently held by the calling thread (or if passed NULL). Intended for use in assert().
requirements: Only available when not compiled with NDEBUG; otherwise may be stub
Return 1 for NULL pointer

functions.name: sqlite3_mutex_notheld
functions.description: For debug builds, returns true if the mutex is not held by the calling thread (or if passed NULL). Intended for use in assert().
requirements: Only available when not compiled with NDEBUG; otherwise may be stub
Return 1 for NULL pointer

functions.name: sqlite3_db_mutex
functions.description: Returns the mutex used by a database connection in Serialized threading mode; otherwise NULL.
requirements: db must be valid
Only useful when SQLITE_THREADSAFE and serialized mode

functions.name: sqlite3_limit
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_limit(sqlite3*, int id, int newVal);
functions.description: Gets/sets connection-specific run-time limits (SQL length, max column count, like-pattern length, etc.). Pass newVal<0 to query without changing. Returns prior value regardless.
requirements: db must be valid
id must be one of SQLITE_LIMIT_* constants

functions.name: sqlite3_status
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_status(int op, int *pCurrent, int *pHighwater, int resetFlag);
functions.description: Reports global status metrics (memory usage, pagecache usage, etc.). Returns SQLITE_OK. resetFlag non-zero resets the high-water mark where applicable.
requirements: op must be a valid SQLITE_STATUS_*
If pCurrent or pHighwater is NULL, the corresponding value is not written

functions.name: sqlite3_status64
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_status64(int op, sqlite3_int64 *pCurrent, sqlite3_int64 *pHighwater, int resetFlag);
functions.description: 64-bit variant of sqlite3_status().

functions.name: sqlite3_db_status
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_db_status(sqlite3*, int op, int *pCur, int *pHiwtr, int resetFlg);
functions.description: Reports per-connection status metrics (lookaside usage, cache usage/hits/misses, etc.). Optionally resets high watermark. Returns SQLITE_OK or error.
requirements: db must be valid
op must be a valid SQLITE_DBSTATUS_*

functions.name: sqlite3_stmt_status
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_stmt_status(sqlite3_stmt*, int op, int resetFlg);
functions.description: Reports per-statement counters (full-scan steps, sorts, VM steps, etc.). If resetFlg non-zero, counter is reset after read (except MEMUSED).
requirements: pStmt must be valid
op must be SQLITE_STMTSTATUS_*

functions.name: sqlite3_stmt_scanstatus
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_stmt_scanstatus(sqlite3_stmt *pStmt, int idx, int iScanStatusOp, void *pOut);
functions.description: Returns predicted/measured performance data for the idx-th loop in the query plan when compiled with SQLITE_ENABLE_STMT_SCANSTATUS. Writes result to pOut based on iScanStatusOp (NLOOP, NVISIT, EST, NAME, EXPLAIN, SELECTID).
requirements: pStmt must be valid
idx must be in range of loops; otherwise returns non-zero and pOut unchanged
Only available if compiled with SQLITE_ENABLE_STMT_SCANSTATUS

functions.name: sqlite3_stmt_scanstatus_reset
functions.description: Resets all scanstatus counters for a prepared statement.
requirements: pStmt must be valid
Only if compiled with SQLITE_ENABLE_STMT_SCANSTATUS

functions.name: sqlite3_file_control
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_file_control(sqlite3*, const char *zDbName, int op, void*);
functions.description: Issues a file-control opcode to the underlying VFS for the named database ("main","temp", or attached). Some opcodes are handled directly by core (e.g., FILE_POINTER, JOURNAL_POINTER, VFS_POINTER, DATA_VERSION).
requirements: zDbName must be a valid attached db name or NULL for main
op must be a valid SQLITE_FCNTL_* constant
Returns SQLITE_ERROR if zDbName not found or underlying xFileControl returns SQLITE_ERROR

functions.name: sqlite3_test_control
functions.description: Internal/testing API to inspect/internal state or inject faults. Not for application use. Behavior and opcodes subject to change.
requirements: Only for testing; do not use in production
Not stable across versions

functions.name: sqlite3_keyword_count
functions.description: Returns the number of SQL keywords understood by SQLite.

functions.name: sqlite3_keyword_name
functions.description: Given N, outputs pointer to the N-th keyword string (UTF-8, not NUL-terminated) in *Z and its byte length in *L. Returns SQLITE_OK on success or SQLITE_ERROR if N out-of-range.
requirements: Z and L must be valid pointers
Returned string must not be modified/freed

functions.name: sqlite3_keyword_check
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the L-byte identifier Z is a SQL keyword, zero otherwise.
requirements: Z need not be NUL-terminated; must be valid pointer

functions.name: sqlite3_backup_init
functions.signature: SQLITE_API sqlite3_backup *sqlite3_backup_init(sqlite3 *pDest, const char *zDestName, sqlite3 *pSource, const char *zSourceName);
functions.description: Starts an online backup from pSource:zSourceName to pDest:zDestName. Returns a backup handle or NULL and sets destination error state on failure.
requirements: Both connections must be open; z*Name must be "main","temp", or attached name
Destination must not have a write-transaction open
Backup handle must be finished with sqlite3_backup_finish()

functions.name: sqlite3_backup_step
functions.description: Copies up to nPage pages. Returns SQLITE_OK (more pages remain), SQLITE_DONE (finished), SQLITE_BUSY/LOCKED (retry later), SQLITE_READONLY, SQLITE_IOERR_*, SQLITE_NOMEM, etc.
requirements: p must be a valid backup handle
Caller should loop stepping until DONE or error; handle BUSY/LOCKED using busy-handler or delays

functions.name: sqlite3_backup_finish
functions.description: Finishes a backup, releasing resources. Commits destination transaction if appropriate. Returns SQLITE_OK if no errors occurred during stepping; otherwise last error.
requirements: p must be a valid backup handle (NULL is a no-op)

functions.name: sqlite3_backup_remaining
functions.description: Returns remaining pages to be backed up as of the most recent sqlite3_backup_step().
requirements: p must be valid

functions.name: sqlite3_backup_pagecount
functions.description: Returns total number of pages in the source database at the conclusion of the most recent sqlite3_backup_step().
requirements: p must be valid

functions.name: sqlite3_blob_open
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_blob_open(sqlite3*, const char *zDb, const char *zTable, const char *zColumn, sqlite3_int64 iRow, int flags, sqlite3_blob **ppBlob);
functions.description: Opens a BLOB handle for incremental I/O on one row’s BLOB/TEXT column. flags non-zero for read-write, zero for read-only. Returns SQLITE_OK or error (e.g., NOTFOUND, READONLY, CONSTRAINT conditions).
requirements: zDb must be database name ("main","temp", or attached)
zTable must exist and not be WITHOUT ROWID
zColumn must be a BLOB or TEXT column; in indexed PK read-write is disallowed
iRow must identify an existing row (except see errors)
Close with sqlite3_blob_close()

functions.name: sqlite3_blob_reopen
functions.description: Moves an open BLOB handle to refer to a different row (same table/column). On failure, the BLOB is aborted and future operations return SQLITE_ABORT; sqlite3_blob_bytes() returns 0.
requirements: BLOB must be open
Target row must exist and type must be compatible

functions.name: sqlite3_blob_close
functions.description: Closes a BLOB handle. If last write and in auto-commit and no other write handles, commits; otherwise may roll back on error. Non-NULL handle is always closed even on error.
requirements: Argument may be NULL (no-op)

functions.name: sqlite3_blob_bytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the BLOB. For aborted handles returns 0.
requirements: Handle must be open

functions.name: sqlite3_blob_read
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_blob_read(sqlite3_blob *, void *Z, int N, int iOffset);
functions.description: Reads N bytes from the BLOB starting at iOffset into Z. Returns SQLITE_OK, or SQLITE_ERROR if iOffset+N exceeds size, SQLITE_ABORT if BLOB expired, or other IO errors.
requirements: 0<=iOffset and iOffset+N<=size; otherwise SQLITE_ERROR and no data read
Handle must be open; aborted handles return SQLITE_ABORT
Z must point to writable buffer of at least N bytes

functions.name: sqlite3_blob_write
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_blob_write(sqlite3_blob *, const void *z, int n, int iOffset);
functions.description: Writes n bytes from z into the BLOB at iOffset. Requires write-open handle. Fails with READONLY if not opened for write; SQLITE_ERROR if beyond end; SQLITE_ABORT if expired; and may violate constraints (reported as SQLITE_CONSTRAINT).
requirements: Open BLOB with flags!=0 for write
0<=iOffset and iOffset+n<=size
Type and constraints must permit write

functions.name: sqlite3_wal_hook
functions.description: Registers a callback invoked after a WAL commit on a connection (or in place of xSync if synchronous=OFF). Callback signature: (pCtx, db, zDbName, nFrame). Returns previous pCtx.
requirements: Only one WAL hook per connection; setting replaces previous
Callback must return SQLITE_OK; other returns cause the committing statement to report error though commit still occurred

functions.name: sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint
functions.description: Configures auto-checkpointing for all WAL databases on the connection when WAL grows to N frames (PASSIVE checkpoints). Pass <=0 to disable. Replaces any prior WAL hook.
requirements: db must be valid

functions.name: sqlite3_wal_checkpoint
functions.description: Runs a PASSIVE checkpoint on database zDb (or all databases if zDb NULL/empty). Transfers as many frames as possible to the database and resets WAL if fully checkpointed.
requirements: db must be valid
zDb must be attached name or NULL

functions.name: sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2(sqlite3 *db, const char *zDb, int eMode, int *pnLog, int *pnCkpt);
functions.description: Runs a checkpoint in mode eMode (PASSIVE, FULL, RESTART, TRUNCATE) on zDb (NULL => all). Optionally returns WAL frame count (*pnLog) and total checkpointed frames (*pnCkpt).
requirements: eMode must be one of SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_*
db must be valid; zDb must be attached name or NULL

functions.name: sqlite3_enable_load_extension
functions.description: Enables (onoff!=0) or disables (onoff==0) extension loading via sqlite3_load_extension() and load_extension() SQL function. For best security prefer SQLITE_DBCONFIG_ENABLE_LOAD_EXTENSION via sqlite3_db_config().
requirements: db must be valid
Affects both C-API and SQL function

functions.name: sqlite3_load_extension
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_load_extension(sqlite3 *db, const char *zFile, const char *zProc, char **pzErrMsg);
functions.description: Loads an extension shared library zFile and runs entry point zProc (or sqlite3_extension_init/sqlite3_X_init guessed). Returns SQLITE_OK or SQLITE_ERROR, with *pzErrMsg set to malloc’d message (free with sqlite3_free()). Requires enabled loading.
requirements: db must be valid
sqlite3_enable_load_extension() or sqlite3_db_config(...ENABLE_LOAD_EXTENSION...) must enable loading
Caller must sqlite3_free(*pzErrMsg) on error

functions.name: sqlite3_auto_extension
functions.description: Registers a statically linked extension entry point to be automatically invoked for each new database connection opened subsequently. Returns SQLITE_OK.
requirements: xEntryPoint must have signature int x(sqlite3*, char**, const sqlite3_api_routines*) though arg-less prototype used; SQLite passes 3 args on call

functions.name: sqlite3_cancel_auto_extension
functions.description: Unregisters a previously registered automatic extension entry point. Returns 1 if found and removed, 0 if not registered.

functions.name: sqlite3_reset_auto_extension
functions.description: Unregisters all automatic extension entry points.

functions.name: sqlite3_db_name
functions.description: Returns the schema name ("main", "temp", or attached name) for the N-th database on connection db, or NULL if N out of range. String is managed by SQLite and may be invalidated by schema changes.
requirements: Protect across threads if accessing concurrently
Copy if needed long-term

functions.name: sqlite3_db_filename
functions.description: Returns absolute path filename for database zDbName ("main","temp", or attached), or NULL/empty string if not applicable.
requirements: Returned pointer is managed by SQLite; not to be freed

functions.name: sqlite3_db_readonly
functions.description: Returns 1 if database zDbName is read-only on this connection, 0 if read/write, or -1 if zDbName is not a valid schema name.

functions.name: sqlite3_db_cacheflush
functions.description: Writes dirty pages for any open write-transaction on the connection to disk, up to OS/file-lock limitations. Returns SQLITE_OK, SQLITE_BUSY if locks cannot be obtained (one or more DBs skipped), or IO errors.
requirements: db must be valid
Do not rely on flushing all databases if SQLITE_BUSY is returned

functions.name: sqlite3_get_autocommit
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the connection is currently in autocommit mode, zero otherwise.

functions.name: sqlite3_txn_state
functions.description: Returns the transaction state for schema zSchema on connection (SQLITE_TXN_NONE/READ/WRITE), or for the highest state across schemas if zSchema is NULL. Returns -1 if schema name invalid.

functions.name: sqlite3_next_stmt
functions.description: Returns the next prepared statement after pStmt associated with connection pDb; pass pStmt=NULL to get the first. Returns NULL if none.
requirements: pDb must be valid

functions.name: sqlite3_commit_hook
functions.description: Registers a callback invoked whenever a transaction is committed. If the callback returns non-zero, the commit is converted to a rollback. Returns prior callback context pointer.
requirements: Callback must not modify the connection (not reentrant)
Registering NULL disables the hook

functions.name: sqlite3_rollback_hook
functions.description: Registers a callback invoked whenever a transaction is rolled back. Returns previous context pointer.
requirements: Callback must not modify the connection (not reentrant)

functions.name: sqlite3_update_hook
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void *sqlite3_update_hook(sqlite3*, void(*)(void*,int ,char const*,char const*,sqlite3_int64), void*);
functions.description: Registers a callback invoked when a row is inserted, updated or deleted in a rowid table (not WITHOUT ROWID). Called after the change is made. Returns prior context pointer.
requirements: Callback must not modify the connection (not reentrant)
Not invoked for WITHOUT ROWID tables, some internal tables, or REPLACE’s implicit deletes

functions.name: sqlite3_autovacuum_pages
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_autovacuum_pages(sqlite3 *db, unsigned int(*xCallback)(void*,const char*,unsigned int,unsigned int,unsigned int), void *pArg, void(*xFreeArg)(void*));
functions.description: Registers a callback invoked before each autovacuum to choose the number of free pages to remove (return value). pArg/xFreeArg manage user context lifetime. One callback per connection.
requirements: Callback must be trivial and must not call into SQLite (not reentrant)
xFreeArg may be NULL; frees pArg when replaced or connection closes

functions.name: sqlite3_unlock_notify
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_unlock_notify(sqlite3 *pBlocked, void (*xNotify)(void **apArg, int nArg), void *pNotifyArg);
functions.description: Registers to be notified when a lock held by a conflicting connection is released, to avoid SQLITE_LOCKED in shared-cache mode. Invokes xNotify(apArg[], n) when the blocker’s transaction ends. Detects deadlocks and returns SQLITE_LOCKED in that case. Special DROP TABLE case applies.
requirements: Use only in shared-cache scenarios
xNotify must not call into SQLite on same connection (not reentrant)
May be invoked immediately if blocking connection already finished

functions.name: sqlite3_rtree_geometry_callback
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_rtree_geometry_callback(sqlite3 *db, const char *zGeom, int (*xGeom)(sqlite3_rtree_geometry*, int, sqlite3_rtree_dbl*,int*), void *pContext);
functions.description: Registers an R*Tree geometry callback zGeom to be used with MATCH operator (zGeom(...)). The callback computes whether the test geometry matches an rtree rectangle.
requirements: db must be valid
xGeom must follow the expected signature and set *pRes appropriately

functions.name: sqlite3_rtree_query_callback
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_rtree_query_callback(sqlite3 *db, const char *zQueryFunc, int (*xQueryFunc)(sqlite3_rtree_query_info*), void *pContext, void (*xDestructor)(void*));
functions.description: Registers an R*Tree scored geometry callback zQueryFunc for advanced queries (MATCH function with scoring and visibility).
requirements: db must be valid
xQueryFunc must use sqlite3_rtree_query_info fields correctly

functions.name: sqlite3session_create
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3session_create(sqlite3 *db, const char *zDb, sqlite3_session **ppSession);
functions.description: Creates a new session object attached to database zDb ("main","temp", or attached). Used to record table changes for building changesets/patchsets.
requirements: db must be valid; ppSession must be non-NULL
Cannot coexist with a preupdate hook on the same db handle

functions.name: sqlite3session_delete
functions.description: Deletes a session object. Must be called before closing the underlying db handle.
requirements: pSession must be valid or NULL (no-op)

functions.name: sqlite3session_object_config
functions.description: Configures a session object (currently SQLITE_SESSION_OBJCONFIG_SIZE to enable/disable computing changeset upper-bound size).
requirements: Must be called before first table attach to modify size setting
pArg points to int controlling/receiving setting

functions.name: sqlite3session_enable
functions.description: Enables (>0), disables (=0), or queries (<0) whether the session records changes. Returns final state (0 or 1).
requirements: pSession must be valid

functions.name: sqlite3session_indirect
functions.description: Sets/clears/queries the session’s "indirect" flag (mark changes during this period as indirect). Returns final state (0 or 1).
requirements: pSession must be valid

functions.name: sqlite3session_attach
functions.description: Attaches a table to the session for change recording. If zTab is NULL, all tables are recorded. Tables must have a PRIMARY KEY; WITHOUT ROWID or NULL PK rows are ignored.
requirements: pSession must be valid
zTab may refer to table name; attaching non-existent table is not an error but records nothing

functions.name: sqlite3session_table_filter
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3session_table_filter(sqlite3_session *pSession, int(*xFilter)(void*, const char*), void *pCtx);
functions.description: Registers a filter callback to include/exclude tables by name when zTab was NULL. If callback returns 0, changes for that table are ignored.
requirements: pSession must be valid

functions.name: sqlite3session_changeset
functions.description: Generates a changeset capturing recorded changes for attached tables. On success sets *ppChangeset (malloc’d) and *pnChangeset (size). Caller must sqlite3_free(*ppChangeset).
requirements: pSession must be valid
Do not free via free(); use sqlite3_free()

functions.name: sqlite3session_changeset_size
functions.description: Returns an upper bound (bytes) on the changeset size that would be generated, if enabled via sqlite3session_object_config(SIZE). Returns 0 by default.
requirements: pSession must be valid

functions.name: sqlite3session_diff
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3session_diff(sqlite3_session *pSession, const char *zFromDb, const char *zTbl, char **pzErrMsg);
functions.description: Attaches zTbl (if not already) and computes differences between the table in zFromDb and the current database, adding the corresponding changes to the session. On error returns code and optionally *pzErrMsg (sqlite3_free() by caller).
requirements: zFromDb must be attached to same connection
zTbl must exist and be compatible (same columns/PK) or SQLITE_SCHEMA error

functions.name: sqlite3session_patchset
functions.description: Generates a patchset (like a changeset but more compact – DELETEs and UPDATEs omit old values for non-PK columns). Caller frees with sqlite3_free().
requirements: pSession must be valid

functions.name: sqlite3session_isempty
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the session has recorded no changes to attached tables, zero otherwise.
requirements: pSession must be valid

functions.name: sqlite3session_memory_used
functions.description: Returns bytes of heap memory currently used by the session object.
requirements: pSession must be valid

functions.name: sqlite3changeset_start
functions.description: Creates an iterator to traverse a changeset buffer. On success *pp set to iterator and SQLITE_OK returned. Caller must finalize via sqlite3changeset_finalize().
requirements: pChangeset must point to a valid changeset buffer of length nChangeset
Do not free buffer until iterator finalized

functions.name: sqlite3changeset_start_v2
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3changeset_start_v2(sqlite3_changeset_iter **pp, int nChangeset, void *pChangeset, int flags);
functions.description: Like sqlite3changeset_start with flags (e.g., SQLITE_CHANGESETSTART_INVERT).
requirements: flags must be supported or SQLITE_MISUSE

functions.name: sqlite3changeset_next
functions.description: Advances iterator to next change. Returns SQLITE_ROW while valid, SQLITE_DONE when exhausted, or error code. Not valid on iterators passed to conflict-handlers.
requirements: pIter must be from sqlite3changeset_start()
After SQLITE_DONE, do not call sqlite3changeset_op() until restarted

functions.name: sqlite3changeset_op
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3changeset_op(sqlite3_changeset_iter *pIter, const char **pzTab, int *pnCol, int *pOp, int *pbIndirect);
functions.description: Retrieves current change’s table name, column count, operation type (SQLITE_INSERT/DELETE/UPDATE), and indirect flag. Returns SQLITE_OK or error.
requirements: pIter must be valid and positioned on a change

functions.name: sqlite3changeset_pk
functions.description: Retrieves which columns are part of the primary key for the current change’s table. Outputs an array of booleans of length nCol in *pabPK.
requirements: Valid only when positioned on a change

functions.name: sqlite3changeset_old
